name: Guisarmiere
description:
You are trained in the use of Great polearms.

While wielding any polearm, you have the following abilities:

  • You may use a half action to make a melee attack with the butt end. The damage die for this attack is a d4. You may spend 1 MP to upgrade one butt attack to use a d6 damage die.

  • Any time you land a hit with a polearm and either beat the creature's Defense by at least 3 or roll max damage, you may spend 1 MP to inflict Injury (this applies to hits with either end of the polearm).

  • If the polearm can be thrown, you may halve its range and use Strength instead of Dexterity to fling it with extreme force, dealing +1d damage on a hit.

Describe how you wield your polearm.

improvements.name: Takedown
improvements.description: Whenever you roll max damage with either end of a polearm, you may roll Strength vs Dexterity against the creature you hit. On a win, the creature is knocked prone.

improvements.name: Brace For Impact
improvements.description:
While wielding a polearm two-handed, you may spend an action to brace it against the ground.

For the next round:

  • You gain +WITS Defense.

  • The first time a creature makes a melee attack against you, roll Strength vs Dexterity instead of rolling Engagement. On a win, the attacker is knocked prone and the attack cannot proceed unless they spend 10 ft of movement.

improvements.name: Polearm Master
improvements.description: While wielding a polearm two-handed, if you make an opportunity attack and land a hit, the creature's movement is stopped and they cannot move further this turn.

improvements.name: Deep Impact
improvements.description:
Whenever you inflict Injury with a polearm, you may spend 1 MP to lodge the weapon in the wound. While the weapon remains lodged, you cannot make further attacks with it, but the creature takes –2 Defense and its speed is halved.

Removing the weapon costs an Action. When a creature removes it, that creature must roll Dexterity vs the creature’s current Injury (they may choose to fail the roll). On a pass, the weapon is removed with no additional effect. On a failure, the creature rolls Injury again, as the removal tears the wound further.
